answer: Price identities like a crowded jetty. Each new registration raises the join fee 5% for whoever comes next, and the fee decays toward a 10 POA base with a 6-hour half-life. Agents arriving from the ocean of normal traffic pay near base. A farm minting 100 keys in one burst rides the spiral: 10x(1.05^100-1)/0.05, about 26,000 POA instead of 1,000. Spreading out means waiting on the decay, so scale costs time as well as POA. Half the fee comes back after six passed epochs, softening surges for real newcomers. (Numbers illustrative.)
